transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Thompson (CrestBank Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Platform), Priya Nair (Security), Ethan Cruz (CTO)

Summary (auto-generated): Redwood demo of Optimize features; focused on batching, prefix and KV cache, and cost modelling for high-throughput summarization. Several security/residency questions raised; agreed to run a benchmark and share pricing/pilot SOW.

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on New Year-eve, appreciate it. quick intros - i'm Sofia, i'm the AE for CrestBank. Arjun is our solutions engineer.
[00:15] Arjun Patel: hi all, hey! we'll jump into a short overview then drill into batching and the kv cache cost model. feel free to interrupt.
[00:32] Lena Thompson: thanks, we'll mostly listen then ask specifics. our main metric is cost per summarized transaction with a 200ms p95 latency target.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: also curious about on-prem / VPC options, we have some data residency constraints.
[00:52] Arjun Patel: yep, we'll cover private deploy implications briefly. so quick context: crestbank wants a high-throughput summarization pipeline, roughly 5k reqs/min at peak, average prompt length ~400 tokens, response ~120 tokens. is that still right?
[01:10] Lena Thompson: that's accurate, those are from Q4 logs.
[01:18] Arjun Patel: great. so batching is our first lever — continuous batching with dynamic batch windows. slide: when you increase batch size you get higher GPU utilization and lower cost-per-token, but you trade some latency. we tune per-route SLOs so critical low-latency routes see smaller batch windows.
[01:40] Arjun Patel: to be concrete, for a 200ms p95 target we usually keep batch wait under 10-20ms for small models, but for larger models you may accept 30-50ms waits. that reduces effective per-token compute by ~20-40% depending on model & quantization.
[01:58] Priya Nair: sorry quick Q — how deterministic is batch timing? we need consistent p95 for SLAs.
[02:06] Arjun Patel: good question — we have a hybrid policy: target batch size + max-wait-time + priority routing. critical routes can skip batching (or go to a low-latency pool). in Dedicated you can reserve pools for low-latency.
[02:25] Ethan Cruz: what about KV cache vs prefix cache? we've seen weird cost spikes on prior infra.
[02:33] Sofia Martinez: Arjun, you want to take that?
[02:35] Arjun Patel: sure. prefix caching is basically storing repeated prompt prefixes and reusing attention states, which helps when you have common system prompts or long user histories. KV cache is storing full key/value tensors for transformer layers to avoid re-computing earlier tokens when doing multi-turn or long context sessions.
[02:55] Arjun Patel: practically, prefix cache helps if you have stable boilerplate prompts — hit rates can be very high, and it's cheap. KV cache hits give the biggest runtime savings for long sessions because we skip token re-computation entirely for cached segments.
[03:12] Marcus Lee: what's the memory implication for KV cache? we can't blow up GPU memory and OOM.
[03:18] Arjun Patel: yes memory is the main tradeoff. KV entries are per-request and per-layer — so with high concurrent sessions you need eviction policies and size-limits. our runtime supports sharded KV caches and configurable TTLs. we showed some numbers — a 32k context length session has larger per-entry size; most customers keep TTL to active session length to bound usage.
[03:40] Lena Thompson: can you show an example cost model? that's the main thing finance will ask.
[03:44] Arjun Patel: absolutely. slide: baseline hosted cost with no caching and minimal batching — we estimate $0.018 per generated token for that workload on a sample open model. with batching and prefix cache we project down to $0.012/token; with an aggressive KV-cache hit-rate assumption (60-70% for multi-turn flows) we can get to $0.008/token. these are back-of-envelope but illustrate sensitivities.
[04:10] Arjun Patel: the key knobs are batch size distribution, cache hit-rate, and model choice/quantization. if you change to a quantized variant (4-bit) you shift the cost curve down further but must validate quality.
[04:28] Priya Nair: security: how are cached tokens encrypted at rest, and can we keep KV store inside our VPC?
[04:36] Sofia Martinez: short answer: yes. in Private deployments the cache and control plane sit in your VPC; for Hosted we offer customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and audit logs for cache access. we'll share SOC2 docs.
[04:52] Lena Thompson: good. also curious about eviction policies — chance of cold starts causing latency spikes?
[04:59] Arjun Patel: eviction and prewarm strategies reduce cold-starts. we can prewarm based on traffic patterns and pin hot sessions to Dedicated pools. worst-case you see a one-off penalty on cache miss but overall amortized latency improves.
[05:20] Arjun Patel: i'll walk a short worked example: assume 5k reqs/min, avg tokens 520 total. baseline throughput needs N GPUs; with batching you increase tokens/sec per GPU by ~2.3x. insert slide numbers ... (demo interlude explaining math)
[06:05] Arjun Patel: okay here's a sensitivity table: x-axis cache hit-rate, y-axis cost/token. at 0% hit-rate cost is baseline, at 50% you're roughly 35% lower cost, at 70% you're approaching 55% lower.
[06:22] Marcus Lee: is this using Redwood's Dedicated pricing or hosted list?
[06:27] Sofia Martinez: the back-of-envelope was hosted list; Dedicated has committed throughput pricing and can be cheaper at sustained load. we'll include a side-by-side in the pricing doc.
[06:37] Lena Thompson: latency numbers — can we meet 200ms p95 with KV cache enabled?
[06:41] Arjun Patel: yes, typically KV cache improves latency for long-history requests because you skip recompute. for short single-shot requests caching offers less benefit. our recommendation is mixed strategies per-route.
[06:55] Priya Nair: any regulatory concerns with caching PII? we need careful retention controls.
[07:01] Sofia Martinez: absolutely — you can configure per-route retention, auto-redaction, and choose not to cache routes that might contain PII. we'll map controls in the security folder we share.
[07:12] Arjun Patel: quick demo time — sharing screen to show Optimize console (note: transcription may mislabel some UI names)
[07:30] Arjun Patel: here's the Optimize dashboard — top-left is batch histograms, top-right is cache hit-rate heatmap, center is cost model simulator. i'm going to flip hit-rate to 60% and show cost delta.
[07:48] Arjun Patel: toggling batching policy from conservative to aggressive shows expected latency moving from 180ms to ~230ms p95 while cost/token drops by ~28%. you can set per-route SLOs so that routes that must stay under 200ms won't use aggressive batching.
[08:10] Lena Thompson: can we export the model of this simulation to spreadsheet? finance likes to play with numbers.
[08:15] Arjun Patel: yes export csv is in the UI; i'll run the benchmark offline too and attach the raw numbers.
[08:21] Ethan Cruz: if we go Dedicated, do we still getOptimize features?
[08:25] Sofia Martinez: yes, Optimize and the console are available on Dedicated and Private. some autoscaling features differ in Private but core batching/caching and the cost simulator work across modes.
[08:40] Marcus Lee: about multi-tenant isolation — we need to ensure other tenants cannot evict our cache or affect latency.
[08:46] Arjun Patel: Dedicated provides tenant isolation and isolated GPU pools. for Hosted we use resource slicing and noisy-neighbor protections and can offer dedicated customer pools as an add-on.
[08:58] Arjun Patel: switching to the cost spreadsheet — here's the breakdown: compute cost, memory amortization, storage for KV cache, and network egress. KV cache storage only becomes material at high concurrency or very long contexts.
[09:18] Priya Nair: network egress—if we keep cache in our VPC on Private, is egress minimized?
[09:24] Sofia Martinez: yes kept intra-VPC, the egress is negligible; hosted requires encrypted channels to our control plane but you can approve peering.
[09:31] Lena Thompson: in your example the KV cache gave biggest wins — what hit-rate should we expect? real numbers?
[09:37] Arjun Patel: depends on UX, multi-turn ratio, and session stickiness. we see 40-70% in conversational banking flows where customers reuse context. for single-shot high-variety prompts it's lower.
[09:52] Marcus Lee: can you simulate our workload?
[09:55] Arjun Patel: yes — that's one of the next steps. we'll take the traces Lena provides, run a 2-hour bench and return the CSV with cost projections.
[10:04] [long demo segment omitted for brevity, including UI clickthroughs, CSV export, and small chart tweaks]
[25:10] Arjun Patel: coming back — security quick notes: we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs per request, and KMS integrations. private deploy supports HSMs for key custody.
[25:30] Priya Nair: good. can you include sample SOC2 report and a network diagram?
[25:35] Sofia Martinez: yes we'll attach SOC2 and an example VPC diagram.
[25:40] Lena Thompson: regarding pricing cadence — we have quarter-end budget for pilots — ideally start Jan 2027.
[25:48] Sofia Martinez: that's doable. we'll aim to have the pilot proposal by Jan 3.
[26:00] [Q&A — various clarifications on TTL, eviction, warm-up]
[32:12] Arjun Patel: one last note on quality tradeoffs: quantization can lower cost significantly but you should run evals on your prompt set; Optimize has a recommendation engine that suggests quantization profiles per-model and workload.
[32:30] Lena Thompson: can we run evals during the bench? include few golden prompts so we can check hallucination/regression.
[32:36] Arjun Patel: absolutely — please include the golden set when you send prompts.
[32:42] Ethan Cruz: any competitors we should be wary of? we were evaluating ModelOps Inc and big cloud vendors.
[32:48] Sofia Martinez: yes we listed a few — our differentiator is production-first controls and unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[32:58] Marcus Lee: last operational question — if cache TTLs are high and memory grows, will Redwood autoscale?
[33:05] Arjun Patel: yes, Dedicated autoscaling can provision more GPU memory backing pools; Private has autoscale hooks but depends on customer infra. we also support soft-limits and eviction to keep stability.
[33:20] [wrap-up] Sofia Martinez: recap — Arjun will run bench, Sofia will send pricing and SOW, Priya to share compliance details, Lena to share prompt traces + golden set. proposed pilot kickoff first week of Jan.
[33:40] Lena Thompson: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[33:44] Ethan Cruz: thanks, happy new year.
[33:47] Sofia Martinez: happy new year — we'll get notes and files out by Monday.
[33:54] [meeting ended]

Notes: transcript contains minor ASR errors and UI name mismatches. References to slides and spreadsheets were made. Attachments promised: cost spreadsheet CSV, SOC2 doc, VPC diagram, pilot SOW draft.
